fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Open Lawn Area; Walkway; Landscaped Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Detached Structure; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders identify the property quickly from the road.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the driveway to maintain clear vehicle passage and overhead clearance for emergency apparatus.
• Cut back dense vegetation bordering the walkway to keep a clear path to the front door.
• Mark or identify the single driveway access point clearly so responders arriving under low-visibility conditions can locate it without delay.
• Keep the area in front of the detached structure clear of vegetation and stored materials so responders can reach and work around it.
• Trim vegetation growing close to the detached structure so responders can move around its perimeter without obstruction.
• Install a gate, latch, or clearly marked opening in the perimeter fencing to provide a secondary route to the rear of the property.
• Keep any rear fence gate unlocked or secured with a breakaway latch so responders can reach the back of the property without delay.
• Mark the rear gate location with a reflective indicator visible from outside the fence line.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of stored items so it can serve as a staging area for emergency equipment.
• Cut back vegetation along the rear fence line to allow responders to move along the perimeter of the property.

wildfire.conditions: Large Trees; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Open Green Space; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Multiple Access Routes; Scattered Shrubs
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches on large trees that hang directly over or touch the house.
• Thin trees within the cluster closest to the structure to create more open space between individual trees.
• Remove or trim shrubs that are growing directly against the base of the structure.
• Keep the area beneath scattered trees clear of dead leaves, fallen branches, and low-growing plants.
• Maintain open spacing between the scattered trees and any outbuildings or fences connected to the structure.
• Trim lower branches on large trees near the house up from the ground to reduce the path fire can take from ground plants into the tree canopy.
• Keep scattered shrubs separated from each other and from nearby trees so vegetation does not form a connected path toward the structure.
• Maintain both access routes clear of overhanging branches and overgrown vegetation along the edges.
